newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Lehman wins Florida deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Lehman wins Florida deal.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to 1/4 point softer at midday as bid lists circulated and Lehman Brothers captured $189.8 million Florida Board of Education bonds.
Lehman won the full faith and credit State Board of Education capital outlay bonds with a true interest cost of 5.077 percent.
One trader called the deal "awfully lofty."
"I thought it was very aggressive, but we expected that coming competitively like that," he said.

The trader, however, said the deal appeared to garner "good interest," in at least half the maturities. Bonds in 1998 came as a sealed bid, while bonds in 1999, 2000, 2011, 2012 and 2014 to 2016 were not reoffered.
"I'm sure it will probably do okay," a second trader said.
Back in the secondary, traders said bid lists--totaling close to $200 million by one estimate--were circulating.
"The two lists that I know that were out were all New York paper, and they were index-related bonds, the majority of them," one trader said.
The trader said he doubted players were selling just to make room for new paper because so little is expected.

"I think you just had some people looking to maybe sell outright and look for an opportunity to re-enter," he said. "They look at this as the high end of the range, and just an opportunity to lighten up, and go to some cash, which I don't think is really the worst idea."

On the other hand, with key economic numbers out of the way, the U.S. Treasury's benchmark 30-year bond may find enough energy to push through a 6.50 percent yield, the trader said. As for Wednesday's muni cash market, the trader judged it unchanged.
A second trader said muni cash was roughly 1/4 point weaker in sympathy with Treasury market softness. He also cited "a reasonable" amount of bid wanteds, adding that "they got decent numbers."
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 9/32 at 100-23/32 to yield 6.57 percent despite bond-friendly inflation data.

The Labor Department reported that the Consumer Price Index for January rose just 0.1 percent, less than the 0.3 percent increase economists had expected. The data further supported the view that the Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady for now.
A trader attributed the bond's failure to garner sustainable gains from the data to current high price levels.

"You are certainly at new levels, and we've maintained them for a while, but haven't been able to push through it," the trader said. "So I think, although you've had very good news, that I think you are just kind of taking a breather in here."

Turning to the primary market's negotiated side, Smith Barney Inc repriced $249 million Hempstead Industrial Development Agency, N.Y., bonds, raising the top yield in 2009 to 5.18 percent from 5.15 percent.
Also Wednesday, Bear Stearns & Co tentatively priced $271 million California Public Works Board bonds at a top yield of 5.65 percent in 2016.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 4/32 at 117-26/32. The March T-bond contract was down 6/32 at 113-21/32. The MOB spread was 133 ticks.
--Kathie O'Donnell, 212-859-1655
